articles.author: tessa-wren
articles.title: Game of the Week: Lavender and Blackthorn play for Johto East
articles.dek: The Wails need a win. The Dragons can retain first with a win or tie. Third seed, a home opener and a trip to Cinnabar are all attached to the result.

body.text: Lavender has spent the past two weeks making its passing game look capable of deciding a division. Now it gets precisely that assignment. The Wails host Blackthorn in the final regular-season round, with a win giving Lavender the Johto East championship and any other result sending the Dragons home with the title. Both clubs have secured playoff berths. The difference is whether the postseason starts in their own stadium or somebody else’s.

My pick is Lavender 31, Blackthorn 27. Moth Ball threw five touchdown passes in the 51–10 win at Violet, and Hobbes added 116 rushing yards and two scores. Blackthorn answered its own difficult previous week with a 27–19 victory at Mahogany. Hatterene completed twenty-one of twenty-eight passes for 275 yards and two touchdowns there. These are two passing games with fresh evidence of production, meeting in a game where the standings give neither staff a reason to save its best ideas.
One result changes two playoff assignments

Blackthorn enters at 12–4, Lavender at 11–5. A Wails victory puts both clubs at twelve wins, with Lavender taking the division through the applicable tiebreak. The winner of the division occupies the conference’s third seed, while the other club finishes fifth. A tie leaves Blackthorn ahead on record, so Lavender needs to win outright. There is no useful draw for a home crowd expecting a division celebration.

The third seed hosts the sixth seed on opening weekend. The fifth seed travels to fourth-seeded Cinnabar. That is a substantial difference in preparation and travel, even before considering which opponent eventually occupies sixth. Vermilion currently holds that position, but Olivine can move ahead with a win coupled with a Volts loss. The full Playoff Race feature carries those branches; this game decides which Johto East club gets to watch them from the division winner’s chair.

Blackthorn’s one-win advantage therefore gives it two acceptable results, a win or a tie. It does not make a cautious offensive approach automatically sensible. Lavender just scored seven touchdowns at Violet. The Dragons will have to make a sequence of stops before they can treat their favorable standings position as protection. A passive first half could turn the arithmetic into something their offense has to repair under pressure.
Moth Ball has several credible destinations

Moth Ball completed twenty-one of thirty-seven passes for 300 yards, five touchdowns and no interceptions against Violet. His protection allowed no sacks. The completion rate leaves room for improvement, but the combination of explosive gains, touchdown distribution and clean possessions makes that passing line especially useful before a game of this size. Lavender created separation without paying for its ambitious throws in turnovers.

Might Guy supplied the largest receiving total: four catches for 122 yards, including a forty-six-yard gain and a twenty-four-yard touchdown. Luvdisc caught eleven passes for 101 yards and two touchdowns. Those lines describe different problems for Blackthorn. One receiver can move the ball a long distance on a small number of completions; another can keep appearing often enough to sustain possessions. Assigning all the defensive attention to either one leaves a productive alternative.

The Wail added three catches for thirty yards and a fourteen-yard touchdown. Unfezant scored on a seven-yard reception. Four receivers caught touchdown passes in total. That makes the coverage assignment more demanding than containing a single spectacular player. Blackthorn needs its secondary to communicate through the full receiving group, particularly after Lavender gets close enough that a short completion can finish the drive.

The Dragons should judge their early defensive work by whether they can make Lavender finish long possessions. A single reception to Might Guy can undo several otherwise sound snaps. Keeping those gains in front of the coverage would force Moth Ball to complete more throws, and his sixteen incompletions against Violet show that the passing game does leave opportunities to end a series. The forecast depends on Blackthorn limiting damage rather than expecting the Wails to stop attempting difficult throws.
Hobbes keeps the passing plan practical

Hobbes carried eighteen times for 116 yards and two touchdowns at Violet, then added a thirty-yard reception. Lavender can ask Blackthorn to defend a productive runner while also accounting for several receiving targets. That combination supports my pick more than the five-touchdown passing total by itself. If the Dragons make the Wails spend a possession running, Lavender has a recent answer that does not require abandoning its best players.

The measurable test is whether Hobbes can again reach one hundred rushing yards without Lavender needing an unusually large number of attempts. His last performance averaged more than six yards per carry. Blackthorn does not have to hold him to nothing; it does need enough short gains to create passing situations in which the rush and coverage can anticipate the same assignment. Repeated easy rushing yards would make the explosive receiving threats harder to manage.

Mr. Clanky remains on the injury report with six weeks remaining. That continuing absence belongs in the evaluation even after Lavender’s large win. The Wails cannot assume that the same protection result will recur against a different opponent. People Eater’s remaining injury counter has reached zero, but that counter alone does not confirm a lineup assignment. Any return should be judged from actual participation, not written into the preview as an established starter change.
Hatterene can keep Blackthorn within one possession

Hatterene’s Mahogany performance gives Blackthorn a persuasive reason to remain aggressive. Twenty-one completions in twenty-eight attempts is a three-quarter completion rate, and 275 yards means those completions did more than avoid mistakes. The quarterback threw two touchdown passes. The Dragons scored twenty-seven points and won by eight, a useful response after the previous round’s heavy defeat at Saffron.

Furret caught six passes for 134 yards and a touchdown against Mahogany. Lavender has to account for that production before deciding how freely it can pressure Hatterene. A defense that commits too many resources to the passer can leave a productive receiver with the kind of space that changes a close game. The Wails need to pressure the throw while maintaining coverage responsibilities beyond the first few yards of the route.

Blackthorn’s running options carry an immediate injury complication. Exploud gained thirty-seven yards on nine carries at Mahogany and now appears with a two-week absence. Sawsbuck still has five weeks remaining. Those reports reduce the grounds for assuming that the Dragons can reproduce the same backfield distribution in the finale. A possible replacement can be discussed as a possibility; the current evidence does not establish who receives every vacated carry.

That uncertainty puts more responsibility on Hatterene’s ordinary completions. Blackthorn may need the passing game to produce the manageable second downs that a steady rushing performance would otherwise supply. Furret’s receiving work gives it an obvious route, but Lavender will enter with that same information. The Dragons’ other targets must make enough contributions that the Wails cannot devote their entire coverage plan to one receiver.
Takeaways could decide which offense gets the last useful chance

Lavender intercepted Iron Jugulis four times at Violet. Dugtrio, Octillery, Mimikyu and Noctowl each made one of those plays. Those takeaways helped the Wails separate rapidly, while Muk added a safety. Blackthorn should prepare for an active defense, but four interceptions against one quarterback are not a forecast of four against the next. Hatterene’s decisions will determine how much of that opportunity exists again.

My first benchmark is a clean turnover column for Moth Ball. The Wails can win a close game through their passing range and Hobbes’s production, but a giveaway would hand Blackthorn a shorter route to the points it needs. My second is holding Furret below another hundred-yard receiving afternoon. Lavender can survive individual Blackthorn gains; repeatedly allowing its leading receiver to move entire possessions would make a thirty-one-point winning total harder to defend.

The expected game is closer than Lavender’s last result because Blackthorn brings a productive quarterback and an immediate championship incentive. I favor the home team’s combination of rushing and receiving options, especially after seeing Moth Ball distribute five touchdown throws without an interception. Lavender 31, Blackthorn 27 gives the Wails the third seed and a home playoff opener, while sending the Dragons to Cinnabar. Blackthorn can reverse that forecast by protecting its possessions and forcing Lavender to complete more plays before each score.
